name: X (Twitter)
headline: Moderate: no app review is documented, but every call costs credits and refresh tokens rotate.

firstTest.text: About 30 minutes to a working sign-in and first post, once you have bought credits.

production.text: No approval step is documented: sign up at console.x.com, create an app, buy credits. Above the pay-per-use read cap, you need Enterprise.

approvalWait.text: None documented. The sign-up and app pages we opened mention no approval, review or wait.

whoCanRegister.text: Anyone with an X account: accept the Developer Agreement and Policy at console.x.com, describe your API use, then create an app.

testMode.text: Prepaid credits only. Post $0.015, post with link $0.20, read $0.005. Limits: 100 posts per 15 min per user, 10,000 per 24 hours per app.

Publish a post for the user

actions.review: None documented. Billed per post returned.

actions.label: Keep the connection alive without asking the user again
actions.review: None. Gives you a refresh token.

actions.label: Read and send direct messages
actions.review: No separate review documented. We marked it sensitive because it reads private messages.

actions.label: Like and follow on the user's behalf
actions.review: None documented. Following and unfollowing is capped lower: 50 per 15 minutes per user.

steps.title: Sign in to the console
steps.detail: Go to console.x.com with the X account that will own the app. Accept the Developer Agreement and Policy.

steps.title: Describe your API use
steps.detail: Fill in the profile prompt: who your users are, that they connect their own X account, and what the agent does. The docs set no minimum length.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click "New App" on the dashboard and enter a name, description and use case. Save every key and secret right away: they show once, and regenerating voids the old ones.

steps.title: Buy credits and set a limit
steps.detail: Add a payment method in the Console and buy credits; there is no subscription or minimum. New accounts may get one-time bonus credits from 2 Oct 2026, though X says they are still rolling out.

steps.title: Turn on OAuth 2.0
steps.detail: In the app settings, turn on OAuth 2.0 and pick confidential (web app or bot, with a client secret) or public (native or single-page app). Each redirect address must match a saved callback URL exactly.

steps.title: Build the consent redirect
steps.detail: Send users to X's consent page with a security check value, a state value, and permission to read, post, see profiles and stay connected.

steps.title: Swap the code fast
steps.detail: Send the one-time code to X's token address within 30 seconds. Confidential clients sign in with the client secret; public clients send their client ID instead.

steps.title: Store and refresh tokens
steps.detail: Access lasts 2 hours. Community reports say each refresh issues a new refresh token and voids the old one, so save the new pair and never refresh one user twice at once.

steps.title: Post within the limits
steps.detail: Post as the user, staying under 100 per user per 15 minutes. Check your credit balance before long runs, since every post and read is billed.

steps.title: Handle disconnects
steps.detail: Revoke the token when a user disconnects. If a refresh fails with a bad-request error, ask the user to reconnect.

blockers.title: The free tier is gone
blockers.fix: Plan a budget: sources report the Free tier ended on 6 Feb 2026, apart from public-utility apps, and legacy free users got a one-time $10 voucher. Add a payment method before you test.

blockers.title: Reports conflict on Basic and Pro plans
blockers.fix: Do not build around them: one report says both stay with an opt-in to pay-per-use, another says Basic moved after 1 June 2026 and Pro after 1 September 2026. Check what your Console shows.

blockers.title: Posts with links cost much more
blockers.fix: A post with a URL costs $0.20, against $0.015 for a plain post. Cap link posts in the agent, or have the user add the link in a follow-up.

blockers.title: Refresh fails with a bad-request error
blockers.fix: Usually the refresh token was already used, the user revoked the app, or the secret was regenerated. Check your store for a newer token, refresh one user at a time, then ask the user to reconnect.

blockers.title: No refresh token comes back
blockers.fix: You left out the offline access permission. Without it, users must reconnect every 2 hours.

blockers.title: Reads stop at a monthly cap
blockers.fix: Pay-per-use allows 3 million post reads per monthly cycle. Past that, X points you to an Enterprise plan with no published price.

agentCan: Write the sign-in flow, state check and 30-second code swap
Store tokens, and refresh before the 2-hour expiry, one refresh at a time per user
Post, read and engage within the per-user limits
Track the cost of each call and stop the agent when credits run low
Draft the developer profile and app use-case text
youDo: Sign in at console.x.com and accept the Developer Agreement and Policy
Create the app and store the keys somewhere safe
Add a payment method, buy credits and set a spend limit
Enter the callback URLs and choose a confidential or public client
Sign in to X as a test user to give consent

drafts.title: Your API use (developer profile)
drafts.body: We are building [product name], an assistant that helps [type of user] manage their own X account. Each user connects their own account through the standard X sign-in and consent screen. With their permission the assistant drafts posts, publishes the ones the user approves, and shows how those posts performed. We do not scrape, we do not post without the user's approval, we do not sell X data, and users can disconnect at any time. We store only the tokens needed to act for each connected user.

drafts.title: App description and use case
drafts.body: Description: [Product name] lets you plan and publish posts to X from one place, with an AI assistant that drafts text for you to approve. Use case: user-authorized posting and basic analytics. Scopes used: tweet.read, tweet.write, users.read and offline.access, so scheduled posts keep working without asking you to sign in every two hours.

drafts.title: Consent note shown before the X screen
drafts.body: [Product name] will ask X for permission to read your profile and posts and to publish posts for you. We only publish after you approve a draft. You can disconnect here at any time, or remove access in X under Settings, Security and account access, Connected apps.

unconfirmed: Whether X reviews apps or use-case descriptions. The docs pages we opened mention neither approval nor a wait, and give no minimum length for the description.
Refresh token lifetime. Official pages do not state one. A vendor page says unused refresh tokens eventually expire but gives no number.
Whether refresh tokens rotate. Only a vendor page says each refresh issues a new one and voids the old one. Treat it as true when coding.
The status of the Basic and Pro tiers. Reports conflict and the pricing page we opened only describes pay-per-use and Enterprise.
Whether the posting limits (100 per 15 minutes per user, 10,000 per 24 hours per app) apply unchanged to pay-per-use accounts. The rate limits page does not split limits by plan.
Which scopes, if any, need extra approval. The scope page lists them with no review notes.
